state.case_summary:
A 36-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a painless lump on her neck for 3 months that has increased in size. She appears healthy. Examination shows a 2.5-cm (1-in) firm, irregular swelling on the left side of the neck that moves with swallowing. There is painless cervical lymphadenopathy. Ultrasound of the neck shows a solitary left lobe thyroid mass with increased vascularity and hyperechogenic punctate regions. A fine needle aspiration biopsy is scheduled for the following week. What is the most likely diagnosis?

What is the most likely diagnosis?

Options:
A. benign thyroid nodules
B. thyroid cancer
C. lymphoma
D. thyroiditis
E. None
F. None
G. None

root.label: Subacute Progressive Neck Mass with Painless Cervical Lymphadenopathy
supporting_facts: firm, irregular swelling on the left side of the neck
solitary left lobe thyroid mass with increased vascularity and hyperechogenic punctate regions on ultrasound
excluded_candidates: Infectious thyroiditis: less likely due to lack of pain and absence of systemic symptoms
Thyroid cyst: less likely due to solid components on ultrasound
alarm_features: increased size of the lump over 3 months

B1.label: Thyroid Neoplasm
askable_discriminators: Are there any symptoms of hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism?

B2.label: Lymphoproliferative Disorder
askable_discriminators: Is there a history of immunosuppression or autoimmune disorders?
Are there any symptoms of lymphadenopathy or splenomegaly?

B3.label: Inflammatory/Reactive Process
askable_discriminators: Is there a history of recent infections or inflammation?
Are there any symptoms of fever or malaise?

B4.label: Metastatic Disease
askable_discriminators: Is there a history of cancer?
Are there any symptoms of weight loss or fatigue?
